subject: Transfer risk mitigation questions for Redwood - DPFlow engagement
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@dpflow.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@dpflow.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:32:00 -0400
Subject: Transfer risk mitigation questions for Redwood - DPFlow engagement

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — DPFlow's legal and privacy teams are running a short transfer impact review before we progress to a PO. I pulled together the high-level items they asked to clarify and hoped you could either confirm or point me to the evidence we should share.

Key asks:
- Do you have an up-to-date mapping of cross-border flows for customer data processed via the hosted API (tokens, embeddings, logs)?
- Are you relying on SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) or an alternative adequacy mechanism for EU->US processing, and can you share the signed SCC addendum or equivalent?
- What technical and organisational controls mitigate onward transfer risk (encryption at rest/in transit, key management, access controls, HSM/KMS usage)?
- Any recent DPIA / TIA summary we can include in our vendor risk file?

If possible, can you provide a short summary and any attachments (redacted) by end of day Tuesday? Our privacy team will review and may have a quick follow-up.

Thanks —
Emily
Emily Carter
Head of Privacy Ops, DPFlow
emily.carter@dpflow.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@dpflow.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transfer risk mitigation questions for Redwood - DPFlow engagement

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Privacy & Security lead) and Karthik (product) so we can give the detail and the right supporting artifacts.

Quick answers up-front:
- We maintain a customer-facing data flow map for hosted and dedicated deployments; hosted API flows are documented and will be included in the TIA summary.
- We rely on SCCs for EU->US hosting by default and can provide the executed SCC amendment for enterprise customers; we also offer Private deployment for customers requiring on-prem/VPC.
- Controls: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, per-customer key wrapping with KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), role-based access controls, auditor-access logs, quarterly config review.
- We'll attach a concise TIA summary and a mapping table for SCC clauses to our controls.

Monica — can you prepare the short TIA summary and attach the SCC mapping spreadsheet and the redacted data flow diagram? Emily — we'll send the files by EOD Tuesday. If DPFlow needs a signed copy of the SCC amendment, tell me the right contact and I'll route to legal.

Best,
Diego
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@dpflow.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transfer risk mitigation questions for Redwood - DPFlow engagement

Hi Emily — Monica from Redwood Security. Per Diego's note, attached are the artifacts you can share with your privacy team: redwood_tia_summary_v2.pdf (concise TIA with residual risk and mitigation table), SCCs_mapping_table.xlsx (mapping of SCC clauses to our contractual and technical controls), and data_flow_diagram.png (redacted per-customer flow for hosted API).

Summary highlights (TL;DR):
1) Data flows and scope
- Types of data processed for the hosted API: prompt and response tokens, embeddings (if requested), minimal runtime metadata (request timestamps, region, model id), and optional customer-provided logs. We do not ingest payment data by default.
- Data residency: primary processing occurs in the region selected at request time (EU region for EU customers); for hosted mode some auxiliary processing and persistence for telemetry may occur in US regions — this is documented in the attached diagram.

2) Legal basis / transfer mechanism
- For EU customers opting for Hosted API, we provide SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) executed as an addendum. The SCC mapping spreadsheet shows where contractual obligations map to controls and data categories. For customers pursuing Private/Dedicated deployments, transfers are typically avoided.

3) Technical & organisational controls (evidence pointers)
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. Evidence: server cert inventory and storage encrypt config (available upon NDA).
- Key management: per-customer CMEK options via AWS KMS/GCP KMS and HSM-backed KMS for Dedicated/Private. Evidence: KMS audit ops summary (extractable).
- Access controls & logging: RBAC with least privilege, SSO audit logs retained 12 months, and token-level access audit traces. Evidence: sample access log extracts (redacted).
- Subprocessors: list included in the TIA summary; subprocessors are contractually bound to the SCCs and undergo quarterly security reviews.

4) Residual risk and mitigations
- We enumerate residual transfer risk (low/medium) per category with compensating controls (SCCs, encryption, contractual subprocess checks). See table in redwood_tia_summary_v2.pdf.

Requested next steps:
- If DPFlow needs the signed SCC addendum, please provide the contracting contact (name + email) and we'll have Legal circulate the doc for signature.
- If you require redacted evidence extracts (logs or certificates), we can produce them under NDA.
- If your privacy team has follow-ups, list them in one email and we'll triage.

Attachments:
- redwood_tia_summary_v2.pdf (attachment stub)
- SCCs_mapping_table.xlsx (attachment stub)
- data_flow_diagram.png (attachment stub)

Regards,
Monica Patel
Lead, Product Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

- For the SCC addendum, please have Legal send to contracts@dpflow.com (attention: Julia Park). We expect to execute within 10 business days if the language is standard.

We will pass the TIA summary to our privacy team today and get back with any minor follow-ups. If we need the NDA to receive log extracts, we'll flag that in the follow-up.

Best,
Emily
